passage:
A science museum showed photos taken by a deep-sea camera. The animals looked strange: some were transparent, some glowed, and some had shapes like nothing on land.
A child asked why people spent money studying places humans could not live in. The guide said the deep sea affects Earth in ways people are still trying to understand. It also reminds us that much of the planet is unknown.
The child looked again at a glowing fish. It seemed like a creature from another world, yet it lived on the same planet.
The exhibit changed the child's idea of discovery. Exploration is not only about space. Some mysteries are hidden under our own oceans.
